comment: Classes can be boring if you don't enjoy content but is a great option to take investments and a good professor to know in the Bschool.

Professor Wu has been teaching investments for a while and has a very structured class schedule and teaching method. He is helpful outside of class if you have any trouble. The class is all lecture (can get boring at times), and there are 2 midterms and a final. Prof. Wu prepares you for the tests well and gives a lot of practice problems.

He is so nice. Quizzes are pretty easy way to get points. You have to actually participate to get those points. He is really accessible outside of class and very knowledgable. He can be a little chaotic and take a really long time to complete just one problem but he is also open to feedback and change. His tests are fair and practice prepares you.

Super nice guy and helpful outside of class. I met with him in person but he also replies to emails almost immediately. He tries to teach so that it's not too overwhelming as it is a requirement for all B school students. Tough grader on tests but you will almost exactly what will be on it. His practice tests and problems are extremely helpful.

Dr. Wu is the most organized professor I've ever had. His notes packets are very clear, and you always know what is assigned to you. When he lectures, it feels like he really respect the time of his students. He explains the material really well. Attendance is a must.
A good teacher. Give materials and good lectures. Recommend.

Teaches well. Posts video lectures after class. Tests are open notes. You can even discuss the quizzes with him. Just make sure you understand what you're studying and this should be an easy A with him.

Professor Wu is very kind and is always available outside class for questions/office hours. There's weekly homework but usually really short. He has a review before every exam, and his review sheets are quite similar to the actual exam. He requires a coursepack, but it's actually not necessary because he prints out the note for every class.
Class is mostly straightforward and boring, nothing special. He tries to listen and involve the class. All the material you need to learn is provided. You will need to study for the exams.

One of the toughest graders I had. Wants a specific answer to open ended questions. So, even if your answer is correct, if its not the one he wants, you get points off. The questions on his exams are also very different from practice questions

He has good experience in the financial market and makes the class more interesting by relating the topics to real life. His lectures are clear and easy to follow and he is a nice guy. He walks you through everything to help you understand the topics.
